correctness.rationale: The cyclic host avoids 11 across the join, but the required n-factors need only avoid it internally. A closed walk in the order-(n-1) overlap graph spells the cyclic host by reading the first letter at each step: overlap identifies the subsequent letters modulo the walk length. Conversely the successive windows of a cover traverse all arcs. Strong connectivity follows by going through all zeros. Removing one copy of every arc leaves a nonnegative integer flow of divergence +1 at vertices starting 0 and ending 1, -1 at vertices starting 1 and ending 0. Decompose into unit source-to-sink paths and cycles; r initial zeros force at least r steps on each such path. Appending r zeros achieves r and matches each sink bijectively by reversing the move on its terminal run. Connectivity and balance give an Euler tour. Independently, with m=n-1, for k=1,...,m-1 there are F_(m-k) sources with at least k leading zeros (choose an internally admissible suffix ending in 1). Summing yields F_(m+1)-1; the empty sum at n=2 is correct. There are F_(n+2) required arcs, hence the stated length and surplus. A separate literal cyclic-word enumeration (`python3 /workspace/branches/frozen_math_checks.py`) confirmed minima 3, 6, 10, 17 for n=2 through 5; it is not used for the all-order conclusion.
